purpose: The fourteen real questions asked of this corpus, each with the exact formal predicate that is actually certifiable, the authorities permitted to decide it, what completeness the negative certificate requires, and which of the three kinds of claim it makes. A consumer reads the claim_type before believing anything.
hard_rule: A negative certificate by absence is valid ONLY when the authority is complete for P over every member of the group. Otherwise the answer is UNKNOWN. If Q cannot be certified but P can, the certificate reports P and says so explicitly; it never answers Q with P silently.

claim_types.WORLD_CLAIM: A statement about the world. 'These bytes are identical.' 'A package manager installed this.'
claim_types.CORPUS_CLAIM: A statement about what this corpus records. 'No .blend is indexed under here.' Says nothing about what exists off-index.
claim_types.POLICY_CLAIM: A statement true by a rule we wrote. Complete by construction, therefore always certifiable, therefore the most dangerous to mistake for a fact.

audit_history: Two passes. The first found 11 of 14 queries able to certify a negative. The adversarial second pass narrowed every predicate to what its evidence actually supports and the count fell to 8, of which exactly ONE is a WORLD_CLAIM.

contracts.Q: De que cliente o comision es?
contracts.P: Is every member's container_root inside the declared set of roots for client X?
contracts.completeness: The root->client map must cover every container in the group. Measured coverage: 7 of 101 containers. A container may also hold work for two clients: shared library items span 9 roots.
contracts.certifies_no: client X not in the group's container_roots -- narrowed to 'no member sits under a folder named X'
contracts.unknown_when: |container_roots| > 1, or the map does not cover a present root
reopen_when: the operator declares a container->client mapping
a container is found to hold two clients
contracts.audit_note: container_root decides provenance, never meaning. The folder->client step is a separate authority.

contracts.P: Does the group contain a file whose extension is in the declared 3D format set D?
contracts.completeness: D must be exhaustive over the 3D formats actually used, and the scan must cover every member. MEASURED FAILURE of the first version: D={.blend} covered only 70.1% of 3D files, and 5 projects hold a 3D format with no .blend at all, so the negative was unsound rather than imprecise. D is now declared and audited.
contracts.certifies_no: no member's extension is in D, AND the extension authority covered every member
contracts.unknown_when: partial coverage, or some but not all members carry a 3D format
reopen_when: a 3D format outside D appears in the corpus
magic-byte confirmation becomes available
a 3D work delivered only as rendered frames must be recognised
contracts.audit_note: An unmeasured risk remains: a 3D work delivered as a PNG sequence contains no 3D format. The index would not call it 3d either, so the check that found zero such projects is circular.

contracts.Q: De que obra o track es?
contracts.P: Do the group's folder names resolve, in the cached discography, to exactly one track, with zero names left unresolved?
contracts.completeness: unmatched_count must be 0. An unmatched name might be any track, including the one being excluded. The cache states explicitly that absence is not evidence: a name absent from it means the lookup was never done.
contracts.certifies_no: track T not in track_ids AND unmatched_count == 0
reopen_when: a discography is added for a container that had none
a cached track list is superseded by a new release
contracts.audit_note: This is the contract the others should have been written like: it carried its completeness counter from the start, which is why it never made an unsound claim.

contracts.P: Is every member's publication surface inside the declared obra set {posts, reels, igtv}?
contracts.completeness: Three conditions, none currently met in full. (1) The export must cover everything published; it is a snapshot whose `other` files were all written inside a 55 second window on 2026-07-22. (2) The surface->class rule must be total; `other` holds 330 unresolved files. (3) The surface must be the publication channel.
contracts.certifies_no: surface_set is a subset of {stories, archived_posts}
contracts.certifies_yes: surface_set is a subset of {posts, reels, igtv}
contracts.unknown_when: the group touches `other`, or mixes obra and registro surfaces
reopen_when: the operator resolves what `other` is
a newer Instagram export arrives
the archived_posts conflict below is settled
contracts.audit_note: An unsettled internal conflict: the operator's definition is 'a post is what I uploaded as finished work', yet he classed archived_posts as not-obra. An archived piece WAS a finished post. The rule and the definition disagree on that surface.

contracts.Q: Va al portafolio o a la web publica?
contracts.P: Is this piece excluded from publication by the obra rule alone?
contracts.completeness: Complete only for the negative direction, and only within the policy.
contracts.certifies_no: the group certifies as not-obra under q4
contracts.certifies_yes: never -- every post is a work, and which one goes up is the operator's decision
reopen_when: the operator publishes or withdraws a piece
contracts.audit_note: The positive direction is reserved by design, not missing by accident. The portfolio interface exists for exactly this decision.

contracts.P: Does the member carry a non-empty author statement and a date?
contracts.completeness: Trivially complete, because P asks about fields of the archive itself.
contracts.certifies_no: no member carries an author statement
contracts.certifies_yes: never -- carrying a statement makes a piece eligible, not selected
reopen_when: the operator writes a resumen for any piece
contracts.audit_note: THE CERTIFICATE THAT WAS FALSELY SOLID. Reported as '2026 of 2034 certified out with one boolean'. True by construction: we defined eligibility as requiring the statement. The corresponding world claim -- that the work cannot be used in an application -- is FALSE, because the operator can write a statement for any of them in minutes. The absence is a state of the record, not a property of the work.

contracts.P: Does the group's date hull, drawn from a single declared source, intersect the query window?
contracts.completeness: Every member must carry a date from the declared source: undated_count must be 0, or an undated member could fall anywhere and the negative is unsound. Measured coverage: 8 of 2034 archive pieces carry a date; month folders cover 427 of 783 post files; the discography covers 4 of 101 containers.
contracts.certifies_no: the window does not intersect the hull, the hull is source-pure, and undated_count == 0
contracts.certifies_yes: the window contains the whole hull, under the same two conditions
contracts.unknown_when: mixed sources, any undated member, or partial overlap
reopen_when: a date authority extends its coverage
a release date is corrected
contracts.audit_note: A hull over mixed sources is meaningless and the corpus proves it: all 330 files in `other` share a 55 second mtime window written by one export. An mtime says when a byte was written, never when work was shown.

contracts.Q: Que conceptos comparte con otras obras?
contracts.completeness: Unattainable with present evidence. The only available concepts come from a vision model's reading, and a vision extraction is INCOMPLETE, so 'concept C is absent from the union' does not prove no member carries it. A union over an incomplete per-member extraction is an over-approximation of nothing.
reopen_when: the operator declares concepts for a seed set of works
a refutable structural attribute (SVG path names, blend object graphs) becomes the concept carrier instead of a description
contracts.audit_note: Of 1818 archive entries carrying a machine reading, ZERO carry the author's own sentence. A lattice built on those attributes cannot be falsified.

contracts.Q: Que rig llevo a la sala X?
contracts.completeness: Unattainable: the negative would require every show to have its ScreenSetup on disk. Nine files exist and far more shows happened, so 'no ScreenSetup names Berlin' does not show Berlin was never rigged.
contracts.certifies_no: never -- not even the exclusion survives the coverage gap
reopen_when: the operator attests that two setups are the same room re-rigged
the ScreenSetup collection becomes complete for a venue
contracts.audit_note: Measured counterexample against the name as a key: BERLIN 1 and berlin 2 name one place, 59 surfaces against 9, canvas 3043x272 against 1920x1080, ZERO shared surfaces. A ScreenSetup is a dated deployment.

contracts.Q: Que le entregue al cliente Y?
contracts.completeness: No delivery marker exists in the corpus. Version suffixes like _v7 and _final are a naming convention, which is a free feature with no authority behind it.
reopen_when: an external delivery authority appears: an invoice, an email thread, or a folder convention the operator declares
contracts.audit_note: This is the query whose absence costs the most, because it is what a client actually asks.

contracts.Q: Es autoria propia, o lo instalo un gestor?
contracts.P: Does an ancestor of a member carry pyvenv.cfg, or does a member's path contain a site-packages or dist-packages segment?
contracts.completeness: Complete for the POSITIVE direction only. PEP 405 obliges the interpreter to write pyvenv.cfg, so its presence proves installation. The negative would require every route by which third-party material arrives to be covered by those two markers, and it is not: measured on this disk, blenderkit contributes 138 assets and downloaded asset folders 173, plus 314 library dependencies in LYON alone, none inside a virtual environment.
contracts.certifies_no: never -- absence of a Python environment marker is nowhere near 'this is mine'
contracts.certifies_yes: an ancestor carries pyvenv.cfg, or every member sits under an install target
contracts.unknown_when: the negative direction, always; and an unreadable path, which is no evidence rather than absence
reopen_when: a package manifest authority is added, upgrading 'inside an env' to 'installed by pip as part of numpy 2.1'
another package manager's marker is declared
contracts.audit_note: This was reported as the strongest certificate in the table. It is A-grade in exactly one direction, and it is not the direction that answers 'is it mine'.

contracts.Q: Es una copia byte-identica de algo canonico?
contracts.P: Is the member's full sha256 present in the canonical set?
contracts.completeness: Every member must carry a FULL hash and the canonical set must be fully hashed. A sample hash is not an identity and must produce an explicit tie, never a decision. Measured coverage: the repository is fully hashed; the SSD index carries a full sha256 for 112 of 45536 assets, which is 0.25%.
contracts.certifies_no: the hash is absent from the canonical set and every member is fully hashed
contracts.certifies_yes: the hash is present, confirmed against the exact set
contracts.unknown_when: any member lacks a full hash
contracts.verdict: A on the repository, C on the SSD
reopen_when: the SSD is fully hashed
the declared canonical root changes
contracts.audit_note: The only certificate that survived the adversarial pass untouched. One nuance: byte identity is a WORLD_CLAIM, while calling one copy canonical is a POLICY_CLAIM. What prunes is the identity.

contracts.Q: Es registro de obra, o registro emocional?
contracts.completeness: Unattainable: the predicate is not computable on a single member. No text-presence detector has been validated, and even a validated one would not separate a note about a work from a note about a personal process.
reopen_when: a text-presence detector with a MEASURED hit rate exists
the operator labels a seed set
contracts.audit_note: The canonical unresolved case, and the reason the fourth obligation exists. 5899 stories live on disk and 240 ever entered the index, so 5659 records of this kind are outside every index. A fold here is a confession, not a conclusion, and needs a monitor built on features DISJOINT from the missing one.

contracts.P: Does the name appear in exactly one of the declared role sets?
contracts.completeness: The declared sets must be complete over the entities that appear. They are not: 3 venues and 21 productoras are declared, and sponsor is not a class at all -- it exists only as an exclusion list.
contracts.certifies_no: the name is in no declared set -- narrowed to 'not declared', which is not 'not a venue'
contracts.certifies_yes: the name is in exactly one declared set
contracts.unknown_when: the name is in none of them, which is the common case
contracts.verdict: C for the world claim, B for the corpus claim
reopen_when: the operator declares more entities
sponsor is promoted from an exclusion list to a class
contracts.audit_note: Banco de Chile is a sponsor, and today the system can only say it is not an organiser.
